Went through current errors in tool-call flows, mis-shaped JSON output, and higher-than-expected tail latency on longer contexts. Agreed next steps: Redwood to provide updated SDK guide and batching configs; customer to run smoke tests and share logs; SE to run microbenchmarks on dedicated quantized variant.
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-06-03
Start: 14:00 PDT
Duration: ~42 minutes
Attendees: Alex Moore (Redwood AE), Samira Patel (Redwood SE), Jordan Lee (Redwood Solutions Eng); Priya Rao (Nimbus ML), Carlos Mendes (Nimbus PM), Evan Chu (Nimbus SRE), Maya Singh (Nimbus Security)

[00:00] Alex (AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick roll call?
[00:05] Priya: Priya here.
[00:07] Carlos: Carlos here.
[00:09] Evan: Evan.
[00:10] Maya: Maya.
[00:12] Samira (SE): Samira from Redwood.
[00:14] Jordan: Jordan.
[00:16] Alex: Great. So agenda is quick status, dig into the SDK function and tool calling issues you flagged, look at structured output mismatches, and agree next steps. Priya, do you want to give a 2-min update on how things went since last week?

[00:34] Priya: Sure. We wired up the SDK in staging, used the function-calling path for our record-enrichment service. Basic calls work, but we're seeing two classes of problems: one, occasionally the tool call returns malformed JSON - like trailing commas or missing keys - and two, tail latency spikes on requests with longer clinical notes, sometimes up to 900 to 1,200 ms per token? maybe I mean 900-1200 ms total, transcription's weird - basically higher-than-expected. We also hit an auth token refresh bug but that's on our side.

[01:12] Samira: Thanks. On the malformed JSON, are you using the SDK helper that returns structured output or parsing raw completions?

[01:20] Priya: We're using the SDK structured-output helper, calling a function schema we set up. The function is defined in our app as annotate_record(schema) and we pass a JSON schema. Sometimes the model returns an object that doesn't match the schema and the SDK unwrap step throws.

[01:35] Jordan: Quick note: we saw similar behavior when the prompt included lists with bullets; the model would return a stringified JSON in the 'notes' field and that breaks our parser.

[01:50] Samira: Okay, couple of places to look. First, SDK version - are you on 1.4.1 or 1.5-beta? There was a patch improving the JSON sanitizer.

[01:59] Priya: We're on 1.4.0, whoops.

[02:02] Alex: Good catch. We'll send an updated integration guide with the 1.5 SDK examples. That includes the parse preflight that tolerates stringified JSON and does a second-pass parse.

[02:12] Carlos: That'd be great. On the latency side, Evan captured flamegraphs - we saw CPU spikes in your SDK client when it tried to post-process token streams. Might be that we're doing too much client-side reassembly.

[02:29] Evan: Yeah, and when we switched to streaming responses in staging we saw fewer spikes but still occasional tails.

[02:36] Samira: Two knobs to check: batching and prefix/KV cache behavior. If your requests have a lot of shared context (patient metadata) using prefix caching will cut compute. Also, reduce client-side reassembly: the SDK supports server-side structured streaming so you can receive function args as they're emitted and avoid an extra parse pass.

[03:01] Priya: How do we enable server-side structured streaming? I thought the streaming was raw tokens.

[03:07] Samira: In the SDK it's an option on the request: stream=true and structured_output=true; on Redwood's runtime we then emit JSON chunks for function calls so the client doesn't need to reassemble. We'll include example code.

[03:20] Maya (Security): Quick security question - does streaming structured output affect PII handling or logs? We need to ensure the KMS envelope is retained and that partial streams aren't logged in plaintext.

[03:31] Alex: Good call. By default audit logs capture request/response merkle but redacted; streaming chunks are buffered and the same retention and masking rules apply. We'll send the security doc excerpt - note that for Private customers with VPC/on-prem we can disable logging or set custom retention.

[03:48] Maya: Perfect. Please include the exact fields that get logged.

[03:53] Samira: Back to the malformed JSON: if you can share a couple of sample responses we can reproduce. Priya, can you paste one?

[04:02] Priya: Yeah, I pasted one in the channel but here's an excerpt: "{"diagnosis": "I10", "notes": "repeat: patient presents with...",}" - notice trailing comma and notes sometimes contains escaped newlines.

[04:21] Samira: That's actually a model-side generation artifact. The sanitizer in 1.5 will remove trailing commas and attempt to coerce strings to JSON with the second-pass parse. For structured-output we also recommend tightening the schema (required fields) so the model is nudged to return complete objects.

[04:36] Carlos: On the schema tightening, we tried making 'notes' optional to avoid rejection, but it led to missing fields. Should we enforce required and instead on failure fallback to a rerank or ask for clarification?

[04:47] Samira: For production, we typically recommend: required for core fields (id, code, primary_diagnosis), optional for free-text. If the validator fails, have the SDK call the model again in clarification mode, or call a small deterministic enrichment tool you host. That reduces repeated LLM cost.

[05:05] Priya: Makes sense. We'll change the schema.

[05:08] Jordan: Regarding tool calling failures - we saw an error code 502 when invoking internal webhook tool via the Redwood tool framework. The payload was 1.2MB and your gateway timed out.

[05:20] Samira: Gateway timeout could be due to payload size or synchronous invocation. For large payloads we recommend storing the payload in a signed S3 URL and passing the URL as the tool arg. Also, check the tool max payload config; default is 512KB. We can raise that on Dedicated or Private.

[05:38] Evan: We can do S3 signed URLs but we prefer not to put PHI in object storage. Any alternatives?

[05:45] Samira: If PHI is involved and you're on Private or Dedicated, you can use VPC-only object storage or enable an internal carrier endpoint. For hosted evaluation, redacting PHI or using tokenization on client-side before storing is recommended. We'll include a section on secure payload patterns.

[06:04] Maya: Also gating: does Redwood support customer-managed KMS for tool payloads?

[06:10] Alex: Yes, for Private customers we support customer KMS/HSM; for Dedicated we can integrate with cloud KMS per contract. We'll include the KMS integration note.

[06:20] Carlos: Back to latency - you mentioned batching. We have variable traffic; some requests are single-record, sometimes we send micro-batches of 10. How does batching affect function call determinism?

[06:32] Samira: Batching is transparent at the cell level; each request gets its own logical response. But batching can increase tail latency if one item in the batch has a long context. We recommend grouping similar-length requests and using the SDK's adaptive batching config. I'll attach sample throughput configs that worked for a healthcare customer we saw.

[06:50] Priya: Can you share numbers? Example: our baseline single-call p95 was ~650ms, when batching p95 went to 1.2s for mixed sizes.

[06:59] Samira: We'll run microbenchmarks on Dedicated with quantized model and your median sequence lengths. Preliminary expectations: with prefix caching and per-route batching you should see p95 drop to ~400-500ms for your typical loads. But if you push very long notes (5k tokens) it's expected to rise. We'll run tests and share spreadsheet.

[07:20] Alex: On model choice: are you on the curated open model in our catalog or on a custom checkpoint?

[07:26] Priya: Using the catalog variant 'redwood-bison-3b' as a placeholder; we plan to test a quantized 4-bit variant next week.

[07:33] Samira: Quantization helps latency and cost but sometimes increases tokenization edge-case misgenerations that affect structured output. We'll test both and include a quality/regression check tied to your eval set.

[07:47] Carlos: Great. For the eval set, will Redwood run evals or do we run locally?

[07:52] Samira: We can run or provide tooling. For pilot we usually run a joint eval: you provide labeled golden outputs, we run batch evals across model variants and quantization settings and report regressions.

[08:04] Priya: We'll send a 200-record labeled set.

[08:08] Jordan: Quick integration question: when using the SDK's function calling, how do retries interact? If a function call to our webhook times out and we retry the LLM call, do we risk duplicate tool invocations?

[08:20] Samira: SDK supports idempotency keys and best practice is to attach one per logical request. Also use async tool invocation where possible; the Redwood tool framework can return an ack and you can fetch results. We'll add recommended patterns in the guide.

[08:35] Evan: For SRE, we'll need sample firewall rules for VPC peering - which ports, CIDR ranges, etc.

[08:41] Alex: We'll attach the network checklist. Evan, can you confirm whether you're doing classic peering or direct connect?

[08:48] Evan: Peering for now. We'll likely move to direct connect during prod.

[08:52] Maya: Also need SOC 2 artifacts and an encryption-at-rest confirmation.

[08:57] Alex: We'll share SOC 2 summary and a note on envelope encryption and KMS integration.

[09:03] Carlos: One more: when the SDK returns structured output but the model inserts unexpected keys, do we recommend strict schema validation or lenient merging?

[09:12] Samira: For initial rollout, lenient merging to avoid blocking downstream ingestion is safer; create a fallback sanitizer that whitelists keys and stores unknowns in an 'extras' blob. After a month of telemetry, flip to strict mode for quality.

[09:28] Priya: That approach matches our ingestion pipeline.

[09:32] Alex: Alright let's capture the concrete next steps - I'll read them out: Redwood will send updated SDK guide with examples for structured streaming and sanitizer; SE will run latency/cost microbenchmarks on Dedicated quantized variant and share spreadsheet; Customer will run smoke tests and provide sample failure logs and the 200-record eval set; SRE will confirm VPC peering details and firewall rules. Anything else?

[09:58] Carlos: Can you also include a sample signed-URL pattern for secure tool payloads that doesn't require public S3?

[10:04] Samira: Yup. We'll include a pattern for internal object storage + signed URL ephemeral keys.

[10:08] Alex: Cool. Any blockers for next week?

[10:11] Priya: The main blocker is the SDK update path - we can't bump to 1.5 without the updated guide because of some internal wrapper. But we'll try a branch.

[10:21] Alex: We'll make the guide backward-compatible and include migration steps.

[10:25] Maya: We'll review the security excerpts before the next call.

[10:29] Alex: OK. We'll follow up with the docs and action items. Thanks everyone.

[10:36] (end)

Notes on transcription: occasional mis-hearings and shorthand; some technical terms transcribed as 'K V cache' or 'S S O'.
